title: Insulin Pump Program Training Notes: Daily Pump Insulin Behind an Infusion-Set Refill
content:
These training notes answer how the daily pump insulin behind an infusion-set refill on an Insulin Pump Program follows the order and dispensing records of the customer's Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program — the active insulin pharmacy program whose delivery method is insulin pump.

**Q1. What if that program has a recent written order?**
Where a written order dated in the three months before the ship date is on the active pump-delivery insulin pharmacy program, the standard window is replaced with the newest pump insulin dispensing, its insulin divided by its own supply days.

**Q2. What if there is no recent order and the pump insulin item was not dispensed recently?**
Where no such order is on file and the program's pump insulin item — J1817 on the Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Part B Pump Insulin Program and rapid-acting 10 mL vials on any other tier — was not dispensed in the three months before the ship date but was in the six months before it, the standard window is replaced with those six months, their insulin divided by the supply days they cover.

**Q3. And in any other case?**
The standard window stands.

**Q4. When is an order or a dispensing in the three or six months before the ship date?**
When its date is later than the same day of the month three or six months before the ship date.

## Worked readings (hypothetical records)

| Records on the pump-delivery insulin pharmacy program | Daily pump insulin |
|---|---|
| Order dated 2 months ago; newest dispensing 3,000 units of insulin for 30 supply days | replaced with 3,000 divided by 30, which is 100 units a day |
| No order in 3 months; item not dispensed in 3 months; 4,000 units dispensed 4 months ago for 40 supply days | replaced with 4,000 divided by 40, which is 100 units a day |
| No order in 3 months; item dispensed within the last 3 months | the standard window stands |
